scenario: A lane runs the check before pushing -- the only way it ever runs, since it is wired into nothing -- in a worktree or container where origin/master, the DEFAULT range's left endpoint, is absent: a single-branch clone, a fetch that named only the lane branch, an agent worktree off a bare mirror; or it mistypes the range. git log writes nothing, its error goes to /dev/null, the while body never runs, found stays 0, scan returns success, and the caller prints 'clean' and exits 0 having scanned zero commits. The lane pushes a commit whose body carries the retired marker, GitHub creates no workflow run, the check rollup is empty, and fold.sh cannot fold a head nothing has built -- the #101/#123/#129/#139 stall this script exists to prevent, with the instrument reporting success. There is no downstream gate for this class: fold.sh:343 only names the marker as the usual cause AFTER a fold has landed with no CI.
evidence: Measured: `skip_ci_marker_check.sh origin/mastr..HEAD` prints 'scanning every commit body in origin/mastr..HEAD ...' then 'clean', exit 0. Nothing in the output distinguishes 'read 24 bodies, none carried it' from 'read nothing': the count is never printed and git's diagnosis is discarded by 2>/dev/null. grep -rn skip_ci_marker_check over the tree matches only its own usage lines, so nothing else would catch the false clean.
remediation: Make the range a precondition and print what was scanned: n=$(git rev-list --count "$RANGE" 2>&1) || { echo "cannot resolve $RANGE: $n" >&2; exit 2; }, then report n. Add a fixture: a range naming an absent ref must exit 2 with a message, not 'clean'. The three existing fixtures all pass a resolvable range, so this invariant has no failing case today.
note: This is the finding that forces needs-remediation. It shares its fix with P2.

scenario: set -o pipefail is on and grep -qF exits at the first match, closing the pipe. Once a commit-message body exceeds the 64 KB pipe buffer, git log is killed by SIGPIPE, the pipeline status becomes 141, pipefail propagates it, the if is false, and the commit carrying the marker is not reported -- the script prints 'clean' and exits 0.
evidence: Throwaway repo, marker in the first line of the body: 4 KB, 16 KB, 32 KB, 60 KB and 64 KB bodies are all found; a 128 KB body is MISSED, reported clean, 10 runs out of 10. Directly: `git log -1 --format=%B <c> | grep -qF -- "$MARKER"` returns 141 with pipefail and 0 without, while grep -cF on the same input returns 1.
remediation: Take the pipe out: msg=$(git log -1 --format='%B' "$c") || die; case "$msg" in *"$MARKER"*) ... esac. Same edit closes P1.
note: LOW and NOT to be escalated, for a measured reason: the largest commit-message body in the last 3,000 commits of this repository is 10,919 bytes, six times under the threshold. No commit that exists today can hit it. Latent hazard in a new instrument, not a live miss.
